title: Predictive tenant throttling service (soft-fence leases + audit signals)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: As Dedicated capacity usage grows, we observe short, high-intensity spikes from a minority of tenants causing transient tail-latency and headroom loss for committed customers. Existing hard quotas and coarse rate-limits either cause user-visible failures or leave capacity underutilized. Goals: (1) provide throughput guarantees for committed tenants while preserving burst capacity for benign spikes; (2) enforce soft isolation for noisy tenants with minimal customer-visible errors; (3) emit auditable eviction/throttle signals for compliance and post-incident analysis. Proposal: implement a Predictive Tenant Throttling Service (PTTS) that combines short-window traffic forecasting, lease-based soft-fences, and an auditable eviction signal chain. Key ideas: - Short leases: allocate time-bounded soft-lease tokens to tenant lanes (e.g., 30s–2m) that encode permitted throughput and priority weight. - Predictive renewal: a lightweight predictor (moving-window + exponential smoothing, later ML model optional) projects the next lease window's load and allows pre-emptive renewal or graceful tapering. - Soft-fence enforcement: when a tenant would exceed allocated lease capacity, PTTS applies gradual pacing and token-bucket backpressure rather than immediate hard kill; critical workloads can be marked as protected to prefer fallback routes. - Auditable signals: every throttle/eviction decision emits a signed event into the audit stream (tenant_id, lease_id, reason codes, predicted vs observed metrics, decision latency) to satisfy enterprise compliance and for incident forensics. - Integration points: runtime admission controller (fast path), console/dashboard for lease analytics, control-plane policy API (per-tenant SLA/priority), and a fallback fixed-rate limiter for predictor failures. Non-goals: replacing long-term capacity contracts or detailed billing; not a full ML-driven capacity allocator in initial rollout. This ticket covers design, prototype runtime integration, and canary rollout for a small set of Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Service design doc published and reviewed in Confluence (architecture, dataflow, failure modes)
Prototype integrated with serving runtime admission controller that issues/validates leases in the request fast path (sub-2ms median additional latency)
Predictor baseline (moving-window + smoothing) reduces reactive eviction events by >=40% on synthetic spike tests compared to current hard-quota baseline
Audit events produced for every throttle/eviction with tenant_id/lease_id/reason and are visible in Console logs and raw audit-s3
Canary rollout to 2 Dedicated GPU clusters with controlled tenant cohort and guardrails defined (kill switch + fallback rate limiter)
Operational runbook and SLOs for PTTS (p99 decision latency, audit event latency, correct-lease-rate) documented
Security review completed and KMS signing keys for audit events provisioned
